speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Both permanent and term contract workers are in employer-employee relationships which are governed by various employment laws, such as the Employment Act, the Employment Claims Act, Central Provident Fund (CPF) Act and Work Injury Compensation Act.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Having both options for both permanent and contract employment helps to keep the labour market flexible and responsive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Employers may wish to employ employees on term contracts when, for example, the job is available on a short-term or project basis.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: At the same time, some employees prefer to enter into term contracts to meet their own needs for flexibility.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Am I correct to say the Minister has said that this data on freelancers, the proportion of freelancers who would prefer to have permanent appointment, would be collected and published from next year onwards?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second question is on the fixed term contract workers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Ministry consider collecting data on how many of them are currently on fixed term contracts but would prefer or are seeking to move to permanent employment?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Ministry consider collecting and publishing that data on a regular basis?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That may be helpful to assess our effectiveness in generating permanent employment for the economy as a whole.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The Member asked whether MOM would collect similar data for those on term contract, meaning that for those on contract, how many of them would prefer to have permanent contract.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In my reply, I have explained that having both the permanent and the contract employment is important for both the employers as well as for the employees because it is important to keep both options available to keep our labour market flexible, responsive.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But the main point which I have highlighted in my reply is that whether they are on permanent employment or term contract, both enjoy the employer-employee relationship.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, in other words, as long as they are on contract, whether it is permanent or short-term, both are employees of the employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, they are protected under all the employment laws.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If they want to have permanent employment, they can always tap on our Adapt and Grow initiatives, where we will work with them to pursue the employment options of their choice.
